site.name: PlanPrice
site.tagline: Verified B2B software pricing and deals

products.name: HubSpot
products.tagline: Free-first CRM that grows into full sales and marketing suites.
products.description: HubSpot's CRM is free for unlimited users, which makes it one of the lowest-risk ways for a small business to get off spreadsheets. The free tier covers contacts, deals, and basic email marketing; paid Starter and Pro editions add automation, deeper reporting, and advanced sales tools. Pricing is per seat, so costs scale with your team.
products.best_for: Small teams that want a free CRM to start and can upgrade into sales and marketing automation later.
products.similar_to: the Salesforce for small businesses

pricing_tiers.name: Free Tools
pricing_tiers.notes: Unlimited users; core CRM, deals, basic email marketing.

pricing_tiers.name: Starter
pricing_tiers.notes: Sales or marketing starter tools per hub.

pricing_tiers.name: Sales Hub Professional
pricing_tiers.notes: 5-seat minimum; automation and advanced reporting.

pricing_tiers.name: Marketing Hub Professional
pricing_tiers.notes: Full marketing automation suite.

strengths: Consistently rated easy to use and intuitive by a large base of marketing users.
Email marketing automation is a standout, with automated workflows cited as a top reason buyers choose it.
Workflows, lead scoring, and campaign automation are among its most-cited pros.
Integrates tightly with HubSpot's CRM and a large ecosystem of third-party apps.
weaknesses: New users report a steep learning curve from the platform's breadth and configuration options.
Pricing is frequently called expensive, especially the contact-tier model where costs climb as lists grow.
Key capabilities are locked behind higher-tier plans.

products.name: FreshBooks
products.tagline: Simple invoicing and accounting built for Canadian freelancers and small teams.
products.description: FreshBooks is built around invoicing: send estimates and invoices, track time and expenses, and accept payments online. It is headquartered in Toronto and prices in Canadian dollars, which makes it a natural fit for Canadian freelancers, contractors, and small agencies. Higher tiers add team members, automation, and inventory tracking.
products.best_for: Canadian freelancers and service businesses that invoice clients and want accounting in CAD.
products.similar_to: the QuickBooks for freelancers

pricing_tiers.name: Lite
pricing_tiers.notes: Up to 5 billable clients.

pricing_tiers.name: Plus
pricing_tiers.notes: Up to 50 billable clients; proposals and retainers.

pricing_tiers.name: Premium
pricing_tiers.notes: Unlimited billable clients; advanced features.

deal.headline: 80% off for 4 months for new subscribers

strengths: Designed to be usable by non-accountants; ease of use is its most-cited pro.
Customer support is repeatedly praised for responsiveness.
Invoicing is simple and fast, including recurring invoices.
Built-in time tracking lets freelancers log hours and convert them to invoices.
weaknesses: Payment-processing fees over 3% are called high relative to alternatives.
Reporting and customization are limited versus more advanced accounting platforms.

products.name: Monday.com
products.tagline: Visual project boards and workflows for teams of any size.
products.description: Monday.com organizes work into visual boards with automations, dashboards, and integrations for project, CRM, and marketing workflows. Paid plans require a 3-seat minimum, so a solo operator pays for three seats. The free tier covers individuals with basic boards; paid tiers unlock automations and views like Gantt and timeline.
products.best_for: Teams that want visual project tracking and workflow automations without heavy setup.
products.similar_to: the Trello for ambitious teams

pricing_tiers.name: Free
pricing_tiers.notes: Up to 2 seats; basic boards.

pricing_tiers.name: Basic
pricing_tiers.notes: Billed annually ($12/month if billed monthly). 3-seat minimum.

pricing_tiers.name: Standard
pricing_tiers.notes: Billed annually ($14/month if billed monthly). 3-seat minimum.

pricing_tiers.name: Pro
pricing_tiers.notes: Billed annually ($24/month if billed monthly). 3-seat minimum.

pricing_tiers.name: Enterprise
pricing_tiers.notes: Custom pricing; advanced security and support.

strengths: Ease of use is its dominant pro; intuitive interface.
Team collaboration features — shared boards, updates, communication.
Strong project management with visual Kanban and Gantt boards.
Automations reduce manual work across boards.
weaknesses: Simple tasks can require paid add-on apps, so basic functionality feels gated.
Steep learning curve for advanced configuration.
Gets expensive as teams grow; essentials locked behind Pro/Enterprise tiers.

products.name: Semrush
products.tagline: The heavy-duty SEO and competitive research toolkit.
products.description: Semrush is the standard all-in-one toolkit for keyword research, site audits, rank tracking, and spying on competitors' search traffic. It is priced per user and aimed at agencies, in-house marketers, and serious content operations. Annual billing cuts roughly 17% off the monthly rate. There is a limited free tier for casual use.
products.best_for: Agencies and content teams doing serious SEO, PPC research, and competitive analysis.
products.similar_to: the Bloomberg Terminal of marketing

pricing_tiers.name: Pro
pricing_tiers.notes: ~17% off with annual billing.

pricing_tiers.name: Guru
pricing_tiers.notes: ~17% off with annual billing; more limits and content tools.

pricing_tiers.name: Business
pricing_tiers.notes: ~17% off with annual billing; highest limits, API access.

strengths: Reviewer-valued competitor analysis.
In-depth SEO insights.
Actionable keyword tracking.
weaknesses: Steep pricing.
Subscription complexity.
Limited trial utility.
Learning curve for small businesses.

products.name: Shopify
products.tagline: The default storefront platform for selling online.
products.description: Shopify hosts your online store, checkout, and payments in one platform — the reason it powers most new ecommerce businesses. Pricing is USD at list; Canadian merchants are billed in CAD at checkout at Shopify's exchange rate. The Grow and Advanced tiers cut transaction fees and add reporting, while Plus targets high-volume brands.
products.best_for: Businesses selling products online that want a managed storefront without managing servers.
products.similar_to: the WordPress of ecommerce

pricing_tiers.name: Starter
pricing_tiers.notes: Sell via social, messaging, or a simple store; USD list.

pricing_tiers.name: Basic
pricing_tiers.notes: $29/month billed annually; roughly C$50–55/mo in CAD; USD list.

pricing_tiers.name: Grow
pricing_tiers.notes: $79/month billed annually; roughly C$132–140/mo in CAD; USD list.

pricing_tiers.name: Advanced
pricing_tiers.notes: $299/month billed annually; roughly C$517/mo in CAD; USD list.

pricing_tiers.name: Plus
pricing_tiers.notes: High-volume plan; custom pricing starts here; USD list.

deal.headline: $1/month for 3 months for new merchants (Basic, Grow and Advanced)

strengths: Widely rated easy to use; no-code store setup for non-technical sellers.
App-store integrations with apps and sales channels are straightforward.
Stores can be launched quickly.
Regarded as reliable for uptime and checkout stability.
weaknesses: Gets expensive: transaction fees plus paid apps add up beyond the base subscription.
Customization limited without coding (Liquid) or costly apps.
Plan pricing draws complaints; integrations occasionally break.

products.name: Wave
products.tagline: Free accounting and invoicing for Canadian small businesses.
products.description: Wave offers genuinely free accounting and invoicing for small businesses, and it is a Canadian company, so CAD handling feels native. It makes money on payment processing (2.9% + 60¢ per transaction) and optional add-ons like payroll and bookkeeping services. The Pro tier adds receipt scanning and removes ads.
products.best_for: Canadian sole proprietors and micro-businesses that want free bookkeeping and invoicing.
products.similar_to: the Google Docs of accounting software

pricing_tiers.name: Starter
pricing_tiers.notes: Free accounting and invoicing.

pricing_tiers.name: Pro
pricing_tiers.notes: $190/year if billed annually; receipt scanning, no ads.

pricing_tiers.name: Payments
pricing_tiers.notes: Online card processing rate when you accept payments through Wave.

strengths: Quick, easy-to-navigate interface for small-business owners.
Recurring invoicing and automated payment reminders.
Long-term users praise the genuinely useful free plan.
Bank transaction syncing automates bookkeeping data entry.
weaknesses: Customer support is poor — users report being unable to reach a human.
Lacks growth features: no 1099 filing without year-round payroll, no inventory, no time tracking.
Paid add-ons are priced high for businesses outgrowing the free tier.

products.name: QuickBooks Online
products.tagline: The accounting suite most Canadian accountants already know.
products.description: QuickBooks Online is the accounting package accountants ask for by name: bank reconciliation, payroll, invoicing, and tax-ready reports in a Canadian edition. Four tiers scale from a sole proprietor to a larger team, all priced in CAD. Intuit frequently runs steep introductory discounts for new subscribers.
products.best_for: Small businesses that want an accountant-compatible accounting platform priced in CAD.
products.similar_to: the Kleenex of small-business accounting

pricing_tiers.name: EasyStart
pricing_tiers.notes: 1 user; invoicing and expense basics.

pricing_tiers.name: Essentials
pricing_tiers.notes: 3 users; bill management and time tracking.

pricing_tiers.name: Plus
pricing_tiers.notes: 5 users; inventory and project profitability.

pricing_tiers.name: Advanced
pricing_tiers.notes: 25 users; advanced reporting and roles.

deal.headline: 90% off for new subscribers (Lite C$2/mo, list C$20)

strengths: Widely considered intuitive; ease of use among its most-cited pros.
Large integration ecosystem for payroll, payments, and industry apps.
Cloud-based anywhere access from any device.
Invoice creation, sending, and tracking is a core praised capability.
weaknesses: Users report missing features versus expectations, especially advanced reporting and inventory.
Pricing called too expensive, with complaints about rising subscription costs.
Customer support frequently described as poor or hard to reach.
Processing fees considered high; report customization has a steep learning curve.

products.name: Xero
products.tagline: Cloud accounting with unlimited users on every plan.
products.description: Xero is the main cloud rival to QuickBooks, known for clean design and unlimited users on every tier — you pay for features, not seats. List pricing is in USD. Xero regularly offers introductory discounts to new subscribers, but the headline offer and its term change often, so always check the current pricing page before signing up.
products.best_for: Small businesses that want unlimited users and strong bank-feed reconciliation.
products.similar_to: the Mac to QuickBooks' PC

pricing_tiers.name: Early
pricing_tiers.notes: Unlimited users; 20 invoices/quotes and 5 bills per month; USD.

pricing_tiers.name: Growing
pricing_tiers.notes: Unlimited users; unlimited invoices and bills; USD.

pricing_tiers.name: Established
pricing_tiers.notes: Unlimited users; multi-currency and project tracking; USD.

deal.headline: 80% off your first 3 months for new customers

strengths: Clean, easy-to-use interface with a dashboard that presents financial reports clearly.
Bank reconciliation is heavily automated through bank feeds.
Connects to many third-party tools including Stripe, PayPal, and payroll apps.
weaknesses: Support is ticket/email-only with no phone line.
Pricing is seen as expensive for micro-businesses.

products.name: Square
products.tagline: Free point-of-sale software; you pay when you take payments.
products.description: Square's point-of-sale software is free — the business model is the processing fee on each sale (2.6% + 15¢ for in-person payments). Hardware readers are cheap and the ecosystem grows into online stores, appointments, and payroll. Square Appointments adds paid tiers for salons, clinics, and services that book online.
products.best_for: Retailers, cafés, and service businesses that need a free POS and transparent card rates.
products.similar_to: the Shopify of Main Street

pricing_tiers.name: Square POS
pricing_tiers.notes: Free POS software; in-person card processing 2.6% + 15¢ per transaction.

pricing_tiers.name: Appointments Free
pricing_tiers.notes: 1 location; basic booking.

pricing_tiers.name: Appointments Plus
pricing_tiers.notes: 1 location; automated reminders and no-show protection.

pricing_tiers.name: Appointments Premium
pricing_tiers.notes: Multi-location support.

strengths: Simple setup, easy to learn even for staff with no POS experience.
Processes payments easily across counter, mobile, and online.
Built-in reporting gives useful sales and staff insights.
weaknesses: Flat 2.6% processing fee adds up and is considered high at volume.
Depends on internet connectivity; outages can disrupt sales.
Free plan lacks features; customization limited without paid tiers.

products.name: Calendly
products.tagline: Booking pages that kill the back-and-forth email.
products.description: Calendly lets clients book time with you from a link — no more 'does Tuesday work?' email threads. The free plan covers one event type, which is enough for a solo consultant. Paid tiers add multiple event types, team scheduling, reminders, and CRM integrations, priced per seat.
products.best_for: Consultants, sales reps, and teams that schedule a lot of external meetings.
products.similar_to: the OpenTable for business meetings

pricing_tiers.name: Free
pricing_tiers.notes: 1 event type; basic scheduling page.

pricing_tiers.name: Standard
pricing_tiers.notes: Billed annually ($12/month if billed monthly); unlimited event types.

pricing_tiers.name: Teams
pricing_tiers.notes: Billed annually ($20/month if billed monthly); round-robin and admin controls.

pricing_tiers.name: Enterprise
pricing_tiers.notes: Custom security, SSO, and dedicated support.

strengths: Very easy to use; simple booking-link flow for hosts and guests.
Eliminates scheduling email back-and-forth.
Google/Outlook calendar integration syncs in real time to prevent double-booking.
Fast, straightforward initial setup.
weaknesses: Free plan is limited, pushing users toward paid tiers.
Calendar sync issues occur, including missed or duplicated events.
Per-user pricing considered expensive for small businesses.
Lacks Apple/iCloud calendar support.

products.name: Jobber
products.tagline: Job management for home-service businesses, priced in CAD.
products.description: Jobber is built for field-service businesses — plumbers, cleaners, landscapers, contractors — covering quotes, scheduling, dispatch, invoicing, and client communication. It is a Canadian company with CAD pricing, and annual prepayment cuts the monthly rate significantly on every tier. Extra team members cost C$29/month each.
products.best_for: Canadian home-service and field-service businesses managing jobs and crews.
products.similar_to: the Shopify for the trades

pricing_tiers.name: Core
pricing_tiers.notes: Month-to-month; C$29/month with annual prepayment.

pricing_tiers.name: Connect
pricing_tiers.notes: Month-to-month; C$99/month with annual prepayment.

pricing_tiers.name: Grow
pricing_tiers.notes: Month-to-month; C$149/month with annual prepayment.

pricing_tiers.name: Plus
pricing_tiers.notes: Month-to-month; C$399/month with annual prepayment.

pricing_tiers.name: Extra users
pricing_tiers.notes: Per additional team member beyond plan limits.

strengths: Intuitive interface.
Excellent mobile app (rated 4.7–4.8).
Professional quotes and invoices; Client Hub.
Automation features.
Responsive customer support.
weaknesses: Per-user pricing beyond 10 users.
QuickBooks sync is unreliable (dropped line items, needs babysitting).
Basic reporting with no custom report builder.
No geofencing or automatic time tracking.
Manual dispatching; no real-time Google Calendar sync.

products.name: Humi
products.tagline: Canadian HR and payroll from the company now known as Employment Hero.
products.description: Humi (now part of Employment Hero) is a Canadian HR platform covering onboarding, time off, documents, and payroll. The core HR platform is quote-based — you talk to sales for pricing. Payroll is the published piece: $7 per employee per month with a $70 monthly minimum, or a managed-payroll service at $30 per employee per month with a $500 monthly minimum.
products.best_for: Canadian businesses that want HR and payroll in one Canadian-compliant system.
products.similar_to: the Gusto of Canada

pricing_tiers.name: Core HR platform
pricing_tiers.notes: Quote-based; contact Humi for pricing.

pricing_tiers.name: Payroll
pricing_tiers.notes: $70/month minimum.

pricing_tiers.name: Managed Payroll
pricing_tiers.notes: $500/month minimum.

strengths: Intuitive interface even for non-tech-savvy users.
Stellar customer support.
Automates CRA remittance and T4 generation.
Canadian payroll with direct deposit and tax calculations.
Benefits admin (health/dental, RRSPs) and onboarding workflows.
weaknesses: Payroll year-end filing difficulties reported.
Inflexible time-off policies for multi-role employees.
Occasional bugs/glitches.
No published pricing — quote required.

products.name: Ahrefs
products.tagline: SEO toolkit with one of the web's most active crawlers.
products.description: Ahrefs is an SEO and marketing platform offering Site Explorer, Keywords Explorer, Site Audit, Rank Tracker, and Brand Radar, powered by one of the world's most active web crawlers. It is a bootstrapped company founded in 2010 by Dmitry Gerasimenko and headquartered in Singapore.
products.best_for: Marketers and SEO specialists who need backlink analysis, keyword research, and site audits.

pricing_tiers.name: Starter
pricing_tiers.notes: Entry tier; no discounts, no free trial.

pricing_tiers.name: Standard
pricing_tiers.notes: Mid-tier plan.

pricing_tiers.name: Enterprise
pricing_tiers.notes: Annual commitment.

products.name: Plausible
products.tagline: Privacy-friendly web analytics without cookies.
products.description: Plausible is an open-source, privacy-friendly web analytics platform — a lightweight Google Analytics alternative with a simple single-page dashboard. Its script is a fraction of the size of Google Analytics, processes no personal data, and needs no cookie banners.
products.best_for: Site owners who want simple analytics without cookie banners or privacy headaches.

pricing_tiers.name: Starter
pricing_tiers.notes: Up to 10,000 pageviews; free trial available.

products.name: Stripe
products.tagline: Payment processing for online and in-person sales.
products.description: Stripe is a payments platform offering payment-processing software and APIs for ecommerce websites and mobile apps, plus in-person payments through Stripe Terminal and dedicated card readers. Founded in 2010 by Patrick and John Collison; dual-headquartered in South San Francisco and Dublin.
products.best_for: Businesses that need online and in-person card payments with developer-friendly APIs.

pricing_tiers.name: Pay as you go
pricing_tiers.notes: Domestic card transactions; no setup or monthly fees.

products.name: Big Cartel
products.tagline: Simple online stores for independent artists and makers.
products.description: Big Cartel is an ecommerce platform for independent artists, makers, and creatives to build unique online stores and sell their work. Founded in 2005; headquartered in Salt Lake City, Utah.
products.best_for: Independent artists and makers selling a small catalog who want a cheap, simple storefront.

pricing_tiers.name: Gold
pricing_tiers.notes: 5 products, 1 image per product.

pricing_tiers.name: Platinum
pricing_tiers.notes: 50 products.

pricing_tiers.name: Diamond
pricing_tiers.notes: 500 products.

products.name: Pipedrive
products.tagline: Visual pipeline CRM designed for sales teams that live in their deal flow.
products.description: Pipedrive is built around a visual deal pipeline. No free tier; plans from $14/user/mo (USD, annual).

products.name: Zoho CRM
products.tagline: Full-featured CRM at small-business prices, with a free tier for 3 users.
products.description: Zoho CRM packs workflow automation and AI at $14-$52/user/mo (USD). Free for up to 3 users.

products.name: Wagepoint
products.tagline: Canadian-built payroll that handles CPP, EI, and T4s.
products.description: Canadian payroll priced as a base fee plus a per-employee charge: Lite C$20/mo + C$4/employee, Core C$40 + C$6, Plus C$80 + C$10 (fee schedule updated 2026-10-22). Bills in CAD.
products.best_for: Canadian small businesses (roughly 1–100 employees) that want straightforward, compliant payroll without a full HR platform.
products.similar_to: payroll done the Canadian way, without paying for an HR suite you don't need

products.name: Knit People
products.tagline: Canadian payroll and HR on one platform, unlimited pay runs.
products.description: Toronto-based payroll + HR from C$39/mo + C$4/employee (Lite). Unlimited pay runs, bills in CAD.

products.name: Acuity Scheduling
products.tagline: Squarespace's appointment scheduler with payments built in.
products.description: Flat monthly pricing from $20/mo (USD). 1-36 calendars, intake forms, payments at booking.

products.name: Setmore
products.tagline: Free appointment scheduling for up to 4 staff.
products.description: Free for 4 staff with unlimited appointments. Pro from $5/user/mo (USD, annual).

products.name: Trello
products.tagline: Kanban boards for visual task tracking.
products.description: Trello organizes work on boards, lists and cards — the simplest visual project tracker in this directory. The free plan caps a workspace at 10 boards; paid plans remove the cap and are billed per user. The cost trap is guests: multi-board guests in a paid workspace bill at the full seat rate.
products.best_for: Small teams that want a visual board without a project-management learning curve.
products.similar_to: the digital corkboard for team tasks

pricing_tiers.notes: Up to 10 boards per workspace; unlimited cards.

pricing_tiers.name: Standard
pricing_tiers.notes: Unlimited boards, advanced checklists, custom fields.

pricing_tiers.name: Premium
pricing_tiers.notes: Admin controls, workspace views, priority support.

pricing_tiers.name: Enterprise
pricing_tiers.notes: Organization-wide controls; 50-seat minimum.

products.name: Asana
products.tagline: Work management with timelines, portfolios and automation.
products.description: Asana is the step up from a board tool: projects, timelines, portfolios and rules-based automation for teams coordinating across departments. List prices are published in USD; Asana's help centre documents payment in CAD, so Canadian accounts can be billed without a US card.
products.best_for: Growing teams coordinating projects across departments that have outgrown a simple board.
products.similar_to: the project portfolio manager for teams that outgrew Trello

pricing_tiers.notes: Free tier for individuals and very small teams.

pricing_tiers.name: Advanced
pricing_tiers.notes: Portfolios, goals, workload management, approvals.

products.name: ClickUp
products.tagline: All-in-one work app: tasks, docs, goals and time tracking.
products.description: ClickUp packs tasks, docs, whiteboards, goals and time tracking into one per-seat subscription, undercutting most rivals on headline price. The catch is add-ons: AI features are billed separately per seat, so model the add-on before comparing the base price against Asana or monday.
products.best_for: Cost-conscious teams that want one app instead of four subscriptions.
products.similar_to: the everything-app that undercuts Asana on seat price

pricing_tiers.notes: Free tier with limited storage and views.

pricing_tiers.notes: Advanced automation, timelines and workload views.

products.name: Notion
products.tagline: Docs, wikis and lightweight projects in one workspace.
products.description: Notion blends documents, wikis, databases and lightweight project tracking. Paid plans are per user; the Business tier now bundles Notion AI, which used to be a separate per-seat add-on. The free tier caps team workspaces at 1,000 blocks, which real teams hit quickly.
products.best_for: Teams that live in documents and want their project tracker in the same place.
products.similar_to: the team wiki that quietly became a project tool

pricing_tiers.name: Free
pricing_tiers.notes: Team workspaces capped at 1,000 blocks; 5 MB file uploads; 7-day page history.

pricing_tiers.name: Plus
pricing_tiers.notes: Unlimited blocks and uploads; 30-day page history.

pricing_tiers.name: Business
pricing_tiers.notes: Notion AI included; private teamspaces; 90-day history.

products.name: Slack
products.tagline: Team messaging with channels, huddles and workflow automation.
products.description: Slack is the default team chat for small businesses that have outgrown email threads. Paid plans are per active user. Watch the renewal price: Business+ rose from $12.50 to $15 per user at renewals after August 2025, so older guides quoting $12.50 are stale.
products.best_for: Teams that coordinate in chat all day and need message history that survives past 90 days.
products.similar_to: the office hallway, as a subscription

pricing_tiers.notes: 90-day message history; core messaging and huddles.

pricing_tiers.name: Pro

pricing_tiers.name: Business+
pricing_tiers.notes: $18 billed monthly. SSO/SAML, advanced admin and compliance.

products.name: Zoom
products.tagline: Video meetings, phone and webinars under one licence.
products.description: Zoom Workplace bundles meetings with chat, whiteboard and mail. The Business tier carries a 10-licence minimum — teams under 10 pay for 10 — which makes Pro the real small-team tier. Phone and webinar add-ons are priced per user on top.
products.best_for: Small teams whose day runs on video calls with clients.
products.similar_to: the meeting room everyone already knows how to join

pricing_tiers.name: Basic
pricing_tiers.notes: Free tier; 40-minute group meetings.

pricing_tiers.name: Workplace Pro
pricing_tiers.notes: $16.99 billed monthly. 30-hour meetings, AI Companion, 5 GB cloud storage per licence.

pricing_tiers.name: Workplace Business
pricing_tiers.notes: $21.99 billed monthly. 300 participants, SSO. 10-licence minimum.

products.name: Google Workspace
products.tagline: Gmail, Drive and Docs for business, priced in CAD.
products.description: Google Workspace is the email-and-docs suite most small businesses default to. Unusually for this directory, Google publishes Canadian-dollar list prices, so the numbers below need no conversion. Plans cap at 300 users, and Gemini AI is bundled into the standard tiers.
products.best_for: Businesses that want business email on their own domain plus docs and storage in one bill.
products.similar_to: the office suite that starts with your email address

pricing_tiers.notes: Custom email, 30 GB pooled storage per user.

pricing_tiers.name: Business Standard
pricing_tiers.notes: 2 TB pooled storage per user, Gemini included.

pricing_tiers.name: Business Plus
pricing_tiers.notes: 5 TB pooled storage per user, enhanced security and eDiscovery.

products.name: Microsoft 365
products.tagline: Office apps, Teams and business email, priced in CAD.
products.description: Microsoft 365 is the Office suite — Word, Excel, Outlook, Teams — on a per-user subscription with Canadian-dollar list prices. Note the July 2026 change: Business Standard rose from US$12.50 to US$14 on annual commitment, and month-to-month billing runs about 20% above the annual rate.
products.best_for: Businesses standardized on Office documents and Outlook email.
products.similar_to: the office suite your accountant's files already assume

pricing_tiers.name: Business Standard
pricing_tiers.notes: Desktop Office apps plus everything in Basic.

pricing_tiers.name: Business Premium
pricing_tiers.notes: Advanced security, Intune device management, Azure AD Premium.

products.name: Salesforce
products.tagline: The enterprise CRM, with a small-business suite at the door.
products.description: Salesforce is the CRM most growing businesses eventually evaluate — and the one whose real cost is hardest to see. Seat prices are only the start: implementation for a small business runs into five figures, and training is a separate line. The Starter Suite is genuinely priced for small teams; everything above it assumes an admin.
products.best_for: Businesses with a dedicated admin or a growth path that justifies enterprise CRM depth.
products.similar_to: the enterprise CRM with a small-business front door

pricing_tiers.name: Starter Suite
pricing_tiers.notes: Core CRM for small teams; monthly or annual billing.

pricing_tiers.name: Pro Suite
pricing_tiers.notes: Deeper customization and automation.

pricing_tiers.name: Core (Enterprise)
pricing_tiers.notes: Advanced pipeline management and workflow.

products.name: Capsule CRM
products.tagline: Simple contact-and-pipeline CRM for small teams.
products.description: Capsule is the deliberately simple CRM: contacts, pipelines and tasks without the enterprise sprawl. Editions scale mainly on contact counts and pipelines. AI features start at the Growth tier, which is also where workflow automation arrives.
products.best_for: Solo operators and small teams that want a CRM they'll actually keep updated.
products.similar_to: the CRM for people who found Salesforce exhausting

pricing_tiers.name: Free
pricing_tiers.notes: Up to 2 users, 250 contacts, 1 pipeline.

pricing_tiers.name: Starter
pricing_tiers.notes: $21 billed monthly. 30,000 contacts, 1 pipeline.

pricing_tiers.name: Growth
pricing_tiers.notes: $38 billed monthly. 60,000 contacts, 5 pipelines, automation and AI features.

pricing_tiers.name: Advanced
pricing_tiers.notes: $60 billed monthly. 120,000 contacts, 50 pipelines.

pricing_tiers.name: Ultimate
pricing_tiers.notes: $75 billed monthly. 240,000 contacts, 100 pipelines.

products.name: Mailchimp
products.tagline: Email and SMS marketing for growing lists.
products.description: Mailchimp is the default first email platform for small businesses: campaigns, automations and a free tier to start. Pricing scales by contact count, so the same plan gets more expensive as your list grows — the 5,000-contact prices below show the jump. The current 15%-off offer applies to accounts with 10,000+ contacts.
products.best_for: Businesses sending regular email campaigns to a growing list.
products.similar_to: the first email tool most businesses outgrow

pricing_tiers.name: Free
pricing_tiers.notes: Basic email for very small lists.

pricing_tiers.name: Essentials
pricing_tiers.notes: Email plus automations; $75/mo at 5,000 contacts.

pricing_tiers.name: Standard
pricing_tiers.notes: Advanced automations and insights; $100/mo at 5,000 contacts; $135/mo at 10,000.

pricing_tiers.name: Premium
pricing_tiers.notes: Phone support, advanced segmentation, unlimited users.

deal.headline: 15% off your first 12 months (accounts with 10,000+ contacts)

products.name: Klaviyo
products.tagline: Email and SMS marketing priced by active profiles.
products.description: Klaviyo is the ecommerce-focused email and SMS platform. It bills on active (emailable) profiles, not emails sent — a distinction that decides your real bill. SMS is priced per send and costs more in Canada than in the US.
products.best_for: Online stores whose email revenue justifies profile-based pricing.
products.similar_to: the email platform built for online stores

pricing_tiers.name: Free
pricing_tiers.notes: Up to 250 active profiles.

pricing_tiers.name: Email
pricing_tiers.notes: Scales with profiles — about $150/mo at 10,000 active profiles.

pricing_tiers.name: SMS (add-on)
pricing_tiers.notes: US sends are $15 per 1,000; Canadian sends cost more.

products.name: ActiveCampaign
products.tagline: Email automation with a built-in CRM ladder.
products.description: ActiveCampaign pairs email marketing with serious automation and an optional CRM. There is no free plan — a 14-day trial capped at 100 subscribers is the on-ramp. Pricing scales by contact count, and unsubscribed and bounced contacts still count toward your tier.
products.best_for: Businesses whose follow-up sequences are the sales team.
products.similar_to: the automation engine for email-led sales

pricing_tiers.name: Starter
pricing_tiers.cadence: per month at 1,000 contacts, billed annually
pricing_tiers.notes: Email marketing and basic automation.

pricing_tiers.name: Plus
pricing_tiers.cadence: per month at 1,000 contacts, billed annually
pricing_tiers.notes: Landing pages, lead scoring; $189/mo at 10,000 contacts.

pricing_tiers.name: Pro
pricing_tiers.cadence: per month at 1,000 contacts, billed annually
pricing_tiers.notes: Advanced automation and attribution.

pricing_tiers.name: Enterprise
pricing_tiers.cadence: per month at 1,000 contacts, billed annually
pricing_tiers.notes: Custom reporting and dedicated support.

products.name: AWeber
products.tagline: Email marketing for creators and small lists.
products.description: AWeber is one of the oldest email platforms, aimed at creators and small businesses. Lite caps you at one list and three automations; Plus removes the caps. A $4.99/month Hold package pauses billing — a genuinely useful feature most rivals don't offer.
products.best_for: Creators and newsletters that send regularly to a modest list.
products.similar_to: the email veteran for creators

pricing_tiers.name: Free
pricing_tiers.notes: Small-list free tier.

pricing_tiers.name: Lite
pricing_tiers.cadence: per month at 500 subscribers, billed annually
pricing_tiers.notes: $15 billed monthly. 1 list, 3 automations, 3 users.

pricing_tiers.name: Plus
pricing_tiers.cadence: per month at 500 subscribers, billed annually
pricing_tiers.notes: $30 billed monthly. Caps removed; $135/mo at 10,000 subscribers.

products.name: MailerLite
products.tagline: Budget email marketing with a nonprofit discount.
products.description: MailerLite is the budget pick in email marketing. Two June 2026 changes matter: the entry plan was renamed Comfort (top tier is now Power), and the free plan was cut to 250 subscribers and 2,500 emails a month. Nonprofits get 30% off paid plans.
products.best_for: Small lists that want real automation without Mailchimp money.
products.similar_to: the budget email tool with honest pricing

pricing_tiers.name: Free
pricing_tiers.notes: Up to 250 subscribers and 2,500 emails/month (reduced June 2026).

products.name: Moz
products.tagline: SEO software with the original domain-authority metric.
products.description: Moz Pro is the long-running SEO suite built around keyword research, rank tracking and its Domain Authority metric. Our dataset currently captures the Standard tier; higher tiers exist but their prices are not yet in our verified dataset, so they are shown as a gap rather than guessed.
products.best_for: Small sites that want one SEO dashboard without agency pricing.
products.similar_to: the SEO suite that invented Domain Authority

pricing_tiers.name: Pro Standard
pricing_tiers.notes: $99 billed monthly. Keyword research, rank tracking, site audits.

pricing_tiers.name: Higher tiers
pricing_tiers.notes: Pricing not yet captured in our verified dataset — check moz.com for current tiers.

products.name: Hootsuite
products.tagline: Social media scheduling and management, from a Canadian company.
products.description: Hootsuite — founded in Vancouver — schedules and manages social accounts from one dashboard. Pricing is per user on annual billing, and it climbs quickly: the jump from Standard to Professional doubles the seat price, so model your actual poster count before committing.
products.best_for: Businesses posting to several social accounts with more than one person involved.
products.similar_to: the social dashboard from Vancouver

pricing_tiers.name: Standard
pricing_tiers.notes: Core scheduling, analytics and engagement for small teams.

pricing_tiers.name: Professional
pricing_tiers.notes: Advanced analytics, team features and higher limits.

products.name: Sage 50
products.tagline: Desktop-rooted Canadian accounting with payroll bundles.
products.description: Sage 50 is the Canadian desktop accounting line many bookkeepers grew up on, sold as annual licences in Canadian dollars with a separate Canadian price book. Payroll bundles roughly double the licence. It is the non-cloud option in this category — your data lives on your machine, and so does the responsibility for backups.
products.best_for: Businesses whose bookkeeper already runs Sage 50 and isn't moving to the cloud.
products.similar_to: the desktop accounting your bookkeeper refuses to give up

pricing_tiers.name: Pro Accounting
pricing_tiers.notes: Core Canadian accounting; up to 2 currencies.

pricing_tiers.name: Premium Accounting
pricing_tiers.notes: Unlimited currencies, deeper inventory and job costing.

pricing_tiers.name: Quantum Accounting
pricing_tiers.notes: Highest tier for larger desktop deployments.

pricing_tiers.name: Pro + Payroll bundle
pricing_tiers.notes: Pro Accounting with payroll included.

products.name: Zoho Books
products.tagline: Accounting priced per organization, not per seat.
products.description: Zoho Books prices per organization rather than per user, which makes it unusually cheap for teams. The free tier covers businesses under US$50K revenue with 1,000 invoices a year. It pairs naturally with Zoho CRM for businesses buying into the Zoho suite.
products.best_for: Small teams that need several accounting seats without per-seat pricing.
products.similar_to: the per-organization alternative to per-seat accounting

pricing_tiers.name: Free
pricing_tiers.notes: For businesses under US$50K revenue; 1 user + accountant; 1,000 invoices/yr.

pricing_tiers.name: Standard
pricing_tiers.notes: Core invoicing, expenses and bank feeds.

pricing_tiers.name: Professional
pricing_tiers.notes: Multi-currency, projects and inventory.

pricing_tiers.name: Premium
pricing_tiers.notes: Advanced workflows and reporting.

products.name: BigCommerce
products.tagline: Hosted ecommerce with a B2B and multi-storefront ladder.
products.description: BigCommerce is Shopify's closest hosted rival, recently renamed into Core, Growth and Scale tiers. Annual billing carries a discount over monthly. It tends to include more built-in features (and fewer app purchases) than Shopify at the same tier — the comparison worth doing is total cost with apps included.
products.best_for: Stores that want more built in and fewer paid apps.
products.similar_to: the Shopify rival that bundles more in the box

pricing_tiers.name: Core
pricing_tiers.notes: Storefront, payments and core selling tools.

pricing_tiers.name: Growth
pricing_tiers.notes: Abandoned-cart recovery and deeper reporting.

pricing_tiers.name: Scale
pricing_tiers.notes: Priority support and advanced merchandising.

products.name: Squarespace
products.tagline: Design-led websites with commerce on the upper tiers.
products.description: Squarespace is the design-first website builder whose commerce tiers double as an online store. Watch the transaction fee: the entry tier historically carried a 3% fee that disappears on the commerce plans — on real volume that fee dwarfs the plan difference.
products.best_for: Design-conscious businesses selling a modest catalogue online.
products.similar_to: the beautiful website that also sells

pricing_tiers.name: Basic
pricing_tiers.notes: Website with core features; $19 billed monthly.

pricing_tiers.name: Core
pricing_tiers.notes: More customization and analytics.

pricing_tiers.name: Plus
pricing_tiers.notes: Commerce features with 0% transaction fees.

pricing_tiers.name: Advanced
pricing_tiers.notes: Advanced commerce: subscriptions, advanced shipping and discounts.

products.name: Wix
products.tagline: Website builder with a free tier and business plans.
products.description: Wix is the other default website builder, with a genuinely free tier and paid plans that add a custom domain and ecommerce. Our dataset captures the Core and Business plans on annual billing; a free custom domain for one year is bundled with annual Premium purchases.
products.best_for: Businesses that want to start free and upgrade in place.
products.similar_to: the website builder that starts at zero

pricing_tiers.name: Free
pricing_tiers.notes: Wix-branded site on a Wix subdomain.

pricing_tiers.name: Core
pricing_tiers.notes: Custom domain and core business features.

pricing_tiers.name: Business
pricing_tiers.notes: Full ecommerce and marketing suite.

products.name: Lightspeed
products.tagline: Retail and restaurant POS from Montreal.
products.description: Lightspeed — headquartered in Montreal — is the POS for retailers and restaurants that have outgrown a basic till: deep inventory, multi-location and ecommerce sync. Software is priced per location register plan; Lightspeed Payments charges 2.6% + 10¢ in person. Model software plus processing together — either alone misleads.
products.best_for: Retailers and restaurants with real inventory complexity or multiple locations.
products.similar_to: the Montreal POS for serious retail

pricing_tiers.notes: $109 billed monthly. Core POS and inventory.

pricing_tiers.name: Retail Core
pricing_tiers.notes: $179 billed monthly. Ecommerce and advanced reporting.

pricing_tiers.name: Retail Plus
pricing_tiers.notes: $339 billed monthly. Advanced workflows and priority support.

pricing_tiers.name: Lightspeed Payments

products.name: Toast
products.tagline: Restaurant POS with Canadian pricing in CAD.
products.description: Toast is the restaurant-specific POS: kitchen display, online ordering and payroll built for food service. Its Canadian pricing page publishes plan prices in CAD — but does not publish the flat processing rate, so the processing line has to come from a quote before you can model total cost.
products.best_for: Restaurants that want one system for POS, kitchen and online orders.
products.similar_to: the POS built only for restaurants

pricing_tiers.name: Starter (Canada)
pricing_tiers.notes: Core restaurant POS for a single location.

pricing_tiers.name: Essentials (Canada)
pricing_tiers.notes: Adds online ordering and deeper reporting.

pricing_tiers.name: Custom
pricing_tiers.notes: Quote-only tier; the Canadian page does not publish the flat processing rate.

products.name: Deel
products.tagline: Global payroll and employer-of-record for distributed teams.
products.description: Deel is for the specific problem of paying people in other countries: employer-of-record where you have no entity, contractor management where you do. The EOR price per employee is the headline; for a purely Canadian team, a domestic payroll tool costs a fraction of it — Deel earns its price only across borders.
products.best_for: Canadian businesses hiring employees or contractors in other countries.
products.similar_to: the border-crossing payroll for distributed teams

pricing_tiers.notes: Deel carries the misclassification risk.

pricing_tiers.name: EOR Standard
pricing_tiers.notes: Deel employs your hire in their country; Enterprise EOR is $899.

products.name: Housecall Pro
products.tagline: Field-service software for home-service trades.
products.description: Housecall Pro is Jobber's main US rival for home-service businesses: scheduling, dispatch, invoicing and review requests. Team plans cap included users (Essentials covered 5 users in our October check), so confirm the current seat caps before comparing against Jobber's per-plan user counts.
products.best_for: Home-service businesses comparing directly against Jobber.
products.similar_to: the US alternative to Jobber

products.name: Cal.com
products.tagline: Open-source scheduling with a genuinely free tier.
products.description: Cal.com is the open-source scheduling platform: booking pages, routing and round-robin for teams, with a free tier that covers solo scheduling properly. It is the main open alternative to Calendly, and can be self-hosted if your business wants the data in-house.
products.best_for: Teams that want Calendly-style booking without per-seat creep, or that prefer open source.
products.similar_to: the open-source Calendly

pricing_tiers.notes: Core scheduling for individuals.
